url_after_normalisation.method: Exact match on the canonical URL after normalisation (https forced, tracking params stripped, trailing slash and #fragment removed, host lowercased).

content_sha256.method: SHA-256 of the whitespace-normalised article text. Catches syndicated copies under different URLs.

extraction_failed.meaning: Page fetched, but no article text came out of it.

junk.meaning: Text extracted, but it failed a quality rule.

rules.high_link_density: more than 35% of characters inside <a> tags
rules.extractor_disagreement: trafilatura and readability-lxml disagreed on length by more than 50%

publish_dates.scope: articles that were stored (a date is only meaningful for those)

five_shortest.title: Links to CSS colour palettes
five_shortest.excerpt:
A while back I decided to stop using Tailwind for new projects and to just write
vanilla CSS instead.

But one thing I missed about Tailwind was the [colour palette](https://v2.tailwindcss.com/docs/customizing-colors#color-palette-reference) ([here as CSS](https://gist.github.com/jvns/9e59b2cd1fe12601084ba78dded072fe)).
If I wanted a light blue I could just use `blue-100` and if I didn’t like it
maybe try `blue-200` or `blue-50`. I’m not very good with colours so it makes
a big difference to me to have a reasonable colour palette that somebody who is
better at colour than me has thought about.
